newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total seeks further reduction of refinery costs.
newsitem.headline: Total seeks further reduction of refinery costs.

text.p: French energy group Total SA said on Wednesday it was seeking a further reduction of its refinery costs and had as an objective slicing another $2.0 per tonne off the costs between now and 1998.
It realised a similar reduction of $2.0 per ton in 1996.
Chairman Thierry Desmarest told a news conference on the company's 1996 results that Total was available for discussions about a restruturing in the ailing European refinery sector.
He added that Total's French refineries were of an above average profitability and would not be candidates for closures soon.

Desmarest said there were signals from both the French and European authorities that they understood the seriousness of the crises in refineries and would probably allow deals along the lines of a recent pact between BP and Mobil.
In marketing, Total plans to reduce fixed costs by 120 million francs per year in France and reduce the number of sales outlets by 100 per year. It currently has 3,187 petrol stations in France.
